alice.dev: Heads up — saw a ~2.3x tail latency regression on small-batch decode in the canary after the kernel-selection heuristic landed.

carla.ml: Ugh. Is this prefill or decode path? sounds like decode-specific small-batch issue.

alice.dev: Decode only. Prefill perf unchanged. The selector is choosing the new FA-v2 fused kernel for decode even when batch=1 and seq_len=16.

dave.runtime: That makes sense if the selector prioritizes throughput kernels. Can you paste the profiling snapshot?

alice.dev: Pasting nvprof summary from the canary run (decode, batch=1, bs=1, seq=16):

```
Kernel                      Calls  Total ms  Avg ms
flash_attention_fused_v2       120    86.4     0.72
flash_attention_prefill_v1      30    5.4      0.18
kv_cache_read                   150   1.8      0.012
lm_head                          120  10.2     0.085
```

emma.perf: FA-v2 has higher per-call overhead for tiny batches due to extra kernel launches + shared memory setup. 0.72ms avg vs expected ~0.25ms.

ben.infra: The selector uses (seq_len>64 or batch>4) -> choose fused_v2, else fused_v1. But the recent change added a cost model that prefers fused_v2 on GPUs with sm80+ for its better asymptotic throughput; it seems we neglected tiny-batch penalty.

carla.ml: Also KV cache layout changed in the last PR (paged KV buffer) — double-check that fused_v2 assumes contiguous KV and is doing a copy for paged layout, adding to overhead.

alice.dev: I ran a microbench locally to compare variants (batch=1, seq=8/16/32). Results:

```
config         kernel         p50 ms   p95 ms
(batch=1,s8)   fused_v1        0.21     0.28
(batch=1,s8)   fused_v2        0.67     0.91
(batch=1,s16)  fused_v1        0.26     0.35
(batch=1,s16)  fused_v2        0.72     1.05
(batch=4,s64)  fused_v2        1.8      2.4
```

dave.runtime: Clear perf cliff for small decode. We should adjust selector cost model to include a startup cost term (alpha + beta * tokens). Current model only uses asymptotic throughput.

ben.infra: Quick mitigation — force fused_v1 for decode when batch<=2 and seq<=32 or when infer_mode=="interactive". Want a patch?

emma.perf: Also consider adding an internal flag in runtime: prefer_low_latency=true for routes marked interactive. That avoids guessing by seq/batch heuristics alone.

carla.ml: On KV side, if fused_v2 does an intermediate memcpy to flatten paged KV, we can optimize by exposing a view API or implementing a zero-copy adaptor for paged buffers.

alice.dev: I've opened a draft PR with two commits: (1) revert the automatic pref to fused_v2 for small batches, (2) add alpha term in cost model and a route-level low_latency override. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/842

perf-bot: CI perf check: small-batch-decode benchmark baseline=0.28ms now=0.32ms (+14%).

alice.dev: CI shows regression but much better than canary. Need canary re-run after selector change + KV zero-copy.

dave.runtime: Action items:
- ben: hotfix selector rule (canary today)
- carla: investigate zero-copy for paged KV (owner)
- emma: add perf test for batch=1 seq={8,16} to CI matrix
- alice: validate canary after change

ben.infra: I'll push hotfix now and tag @alice.dev for verification.

alice.dev: Thx. Once hotfix is in canary I'll run the per-request latency traces and post flamegraphs.

carla.ml: FYI, I reproduced the memcpy cost: fused_v2 does 2x buffer allocs for paged KV. I have a prototype adaptor that yields ~0.18ms overhead vs 0.65ms.

alice.dev: Awesome. If prototype looks good, do a small PR and we'll fold into 842.

dave.runtime: Good triage. Keep thread updated and add test coverage for selector edgecases.

alice.dev: Will do — will post flamegraphs when canary is up. :thumbsup:

ben.infra: hotfix merged to canary at 1769991287

alice.dev: Verified: canary p95 for interactive route dropped from 1.05ms -> 0.31ms. Closing the urgent loop, leaving follow-ups for KV zero-copy and cost-model refactor.

emma.perf: Nice work. Please add a short perf note in the release notes mentioning the selector alpha term.

alice.dev: Will add it.
